From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Aligning 18mo term conversion + usage-tier mediation (MSA & Exhibit D annotation)

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, Helios is looking to: (1) convert the upcoming renewal from a 12-month to an 18-month term, (2) shift a portion of billing to a consumption- tier for burst jobs, and (3) tighten the audit/evidence requirements in Exhibit D (they want more explicit log retention and export formats).

I attached the requested markup template (Helios_Requested_Markup_v1.docx) and a starter evidence checklist (Evidence_Package_List.xlsx) so Legal has a clear starting point. Quick asks for us internally:
- Can Legal (Karthik) confirm any material language that would block an 18mo term conversion (notice, auto-renewal, early termination proration)?
- Ops (Monica) — are there any platform constraints we need to call out for the consumption tier (min-billing granularity, KV-cache implications, prefix caching impact)?

Samir, please confirm that the evidence items in the spreadsheet align with what your auditors will need (log retention windows, SSO/audit event exports, encryption in transit/rest). If Helios wants, we can propose a short addendum to Exhibit D that standardizes export formats and retention windows rather than reworking the whole Exhibit.

Proposed next step: internal legal call Tues 3/4 at 10am PT to prepare a single marked-up doc to share with Helios by EOD Tues. If that works, I’ll send a Calendly.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Attachments: Helios_Requested_Markup_v1.docx (docx - edited copy), Evidence_Package_List.xlsx (xlsx - starter checklist)

From: Samir Qureshi <samir@heliosdata.com>

Cc: Maya Desai <maya.desai@heliosdata.com>, Helios Legal <legal@heliosdata.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Mar 2025 11:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Aligning 18mo term conversion + usage-tier mediation (MSA & Exhibit D annotation)

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the materials; they look good as a starting point. A couple clarifications from our side:
1) The 18mo conversion is sensitive to our procurement cycle — we need the contract to reflect an explicit non- prorated early-termination calculation (our finance team needs to forecast mid-term churn).
2) For the consumption tier, we need minimum billing granularity at 5-minute intervals and a clear definition of what constitutes a "burst job" (so we don't have ambiguous charges).
3) On evidence, our auditors require: 
  - logs retained for 24 months with a one-click export (CSV/NDJSON)
  - audit events schema (we can share ours)

We’re fine with an addendum to Exhibit D that standardizes retention and export format if Redwood can commit to the format and export latency (max 48 hours).

We’re available for a call Tues 3/4 at 10am PT.

—Samir
VP Product, Helios Data
samir@heliosdata.com

Date: Tue, 04 Mar 2025 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning 18mo term conversion + usage-tier mediation (MSA & Exhibit D annotation)

Naomi / team —

Quick read-through of the ask and initial legal guidance:
- 18-month conversion: OK from a legal standpoint, but recommend we add a short paragraph to Section 2.1 clarifying the effective date and the mechanism for prorating charges on early termination. Suggested language attached (I put it in the docx).
- Auto-renewal: Helios has to explicitly opt-in to auto-renew if we change the base term, otherwise we leave current renewal language as-is. Suggest we surface this as a checkbox in the DocuSign cover page.
- Consumption tier: define "burst job" in Exhibit D as > X tokens/sec for > Y seconds OR as jobs flagged via API header. Ops needs to confirm the thresholds; if 5-minute billing granularity is required we should highlight potential rounding/aggregation windows in the billing table.
- Evidence/Log retention: we can commit to a 24-month retention window and NDJSON/CSV export, but need to align on export SLA (48 hours seems workable). We should also preserve language limiting Redwood’s liability for third-party log ingestion issues (standard).

Next steps I propose for Tue 10am PT:
1) Ops (Monica) brings a short note on billing granularity and any implementation constraints
2) Legal (me) will present the 2–3 suggested contract paragraphs for Section 2.1, Exhibit D, and the DocuSign cover sheet language
3) Naomi will consolidate and send a single marked document back to Helios by EOD Tue.

I’m attaching a lightweight patch: Helios_Requested_Markup_v1_KI.docx (minor edits + suggested wording).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Helios_Requested_Markup_v1_KI.docx (docx - K.I. suggested language)

Subject: Re: Aligning 18mo term conversion + usage-tier mediation (MSA & Exhibit D annotation)

Samir —

Thanks everyone for the call and quick turn. Per Karthik and Monica: attached is a single consolidated markup (Helios_Requested_Markup_v1_KI.docx) that includes:
- Section 2.1 language to cover 18-month effective date and an early-termination proration formula (example included)
- Exhibit D: explicit definition of "burst job" plus a billing table note on 5-minute granularity and rounding behavior
- DocuSign cover sheet checkbox for "opt-in auto-renew" if Helios chooses that path
- Evidence appendix: commitment to 24-month retention and NDJSON/CSV exports with a 48-hour export SLA; we added a short liability carve-out for third-party ingestion failures

Next asks for you, Samir: please confirm (a) that the proration formula works for your finance forecasts, (b) that NDJSON/CSV is acceptable, and (c) whether Helios wants auto-renew to be on or off for this converted term. If all good I’ll route to DocuSign for a one- click sign path.

If Helios Legal wants to route redlines back, please use the attached file (track changes preferred).

Best —
Naomi
